papers.title: Resveratrol alleviates osteoarthritis progression by inhibiting NLRP3 inflammasome response via the AMPK/PPARγ signaling pathway.
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic, degenerative disease affecting joint tissue. Resveratrol (RES), a natural polyphenolic compound, has anti‑inflammatory, antioxidant and anti‑apoptotic effects in chondrocytes and macrophages, suggesting therapeutic potential for OA. The present study investigated the molecular mechanisms of RES in OA treatment through network pharmacology analysis and in vitro and in vivo experiments. Network pharmacology was performed to identify potential therapeutic targets and pathways. An OA cell model was established by treating SW1353 cells with IL‑1β, followed by RES intervention without or with AMPK inhibitor to evaluate the effects on the AMPK/PPARγ signaling pathway, NLRP3 inflammasome response, and extracellular matrix (ECM) metabolism. For in vivo assays, OA mice were established through the destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM) surgery, and administered RES through oral gavage. Histopathological changes, serum inflammatory factors and the expression of target proteins in articular cartilage were analyzed. Network pharmacology identified the AMPK/PPARγ pathway as a key mechanism underlying the therapeutic effects of RES in OA. In vitro , RES activated the AMPK/PPARγ pathway and inhibited the NLRP3 inflammasome response, thereby preserving ECM homeostasis in SW1353 cells. In vivo , RES alleviated OA progression by suppressing cartilage degeneration and synovitis, and regulating serum inflammatory levels. The target protein changes were consistent with the in vitro findings. The present study demonstrates that RES effectively regulates the NLRP3 inflammasome response by activating the AMPK/PPARγ signaling pathway, providing a valuable experimental foundation and potential clinical utility for RES as a complementary and alternative therapy for OA.

papers.title: Next-Generation Sequencing to Identify Genetic Causes of Chinese Patients Affected With Non-retinal Developmental Eye Disorders.
papers.abstract: To investigate the genetic causes of non-retinal developmental eye disorders in 14 Chinese different families, we subjected participants to a specific hereditary eye disease enrichment panel (HEDEP) or whole exome sequencing. We further validated disease-causing variants and performed co-segregation analyses on the available family members by Sanger sequencing. We classified sequence changes according to the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics and the Association for Molecular Pathology variant interpretation guidelines. Fourteen probands with diverse clinical diagnoses were analyzed, including microphthalmia (with or without microcornea and congenital cataract or congenital corneal opacification (CCO), four cases), anterior segment dysgenesis (ASD, six cases)-including Peter's anomaly (PA, one case), PA and microphthalmia (one case), iridocoloboma or aniridia (with microcornea and/or congenital cataract, two cases), and primary congenital glaucoma (PCG, two cases)-congenital cataract (with CCO or microcornea, three cases), and Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome (RSTS, one case). Initial inheritance patterns for 1, 5, and 8 cases were autosomal recessive, autosomal dominant, and sporadic, respectively. We identified 17 (likely) pathogenic variants and one variant of uncertain significance (VUS) in 16 genes, including BMP4 , BCOR , PITX3 , and PAX6 . Among them, eight were novel variants, and two were de novo . We confirmed the pathogenicity of PAX6 intronic mutation using in vitro splice assays and redefined the pathogenicity of the variants of uncertain significance as likely pathogenic. Patients with developmental eye diseases typically have complex ocular and systemic phenotypes, possibly leading to significant visual impairment and high blindness rates. Identifying the genetic causes facilitates early diagnosis and effective treatment and rehabilitation strategies, thereby providing valuable insights for genetic and clinical counseling of these patients.

papers.title: ICU-acquired pneumonia beyond pathogen detection.
papers.abstract: Intensive care unit-acquired pneumonia is often treated as a binary diagnosis, although clinical deterioration, imaging and microbial detection describe different aspects of disease. This Perspective proposes an explicit, graded and revisable assessment of whether a detected organism plausibly causes the current lung injury. The framework encompasses pneumonia arising during ventilation, pneumonia that precedes intubation and pneumonia in non-ventilated ICU patients. It places molecular results within clinical, anatomical, microbiological and host context and uses formal reassessment at 48-72 hours to guide treatment continuation, narrowing or discontinuation.

papers.title: RNA sequencing significantly improves HYDIN diagnosis and defines the effects of common deletions in primary ciliary dyskinesia.
papers.abstract: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia (PCD) is a rare genetic disorder affecting ~1:7500 individuals characterised by recurrent chronic respiratory infections, bronchiectasis, laterality defects, and infertility. While at least 60 PCD-causing genes are reported, approximately 30% of patients remain without a confirmed molecular diagnosis. PCD caused by biallelic HYDIN variants is difficult to diagnose due to a 98% homologous pseudogene (HYDIN2). Additionally, functional ciliary diagnostic testing can be inconclusive due to the lack of discernible HYDIN ciliary ultrastructure defects by electron microscopy. Our aim was to diagnose genetically unresolved PCD patients with strong clinical suspicion of HYDIN defects using RNA sequencing (RNA-seq). RNA-seq was performed on total RNA extracted from patients' nasal epithelium cultured for 21 days at the air-liquid interface. Splicing abnormalities were detected using rMATS and genome-aligned reads were manually inspected using Integrative Genome Viewer. Thirteen individuals had strong clinical suspicion of PCD, normal TEM and inconclusive genetics: 11/13 had a single pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant in HYDIN, 1/13 had no variants, and 1/13 required clarification of variant origin (HYDIN vs HYDIN2). RNA-seq resolved 11/13 (85%) of cases. The same complex pathogenic aberrant splicing events were seen in seven unrelated patients. This abnormal splice pattern was caused by a large 10-kilobase deletion spanning intron 17 to intron 18. RNA-seq increases the diagnostic yield for patients with suspected PCD and has exposed a HYDIN 'hotspot' variant, increasing the observed prevalence of HYDIN-related cases within our genetically diagnosed cohort. Routine PCD genomics testing will now incorporate investigation of this genetic region of HYDIN.

papers.title: Clinical Accuracy and Operational Evaluation of a Novel Nanopore Based 16S Diagnostic Pathogen Detection Workflow.
papers.abstract: Culture-based methods remain standard practice for pathogenic bacterial detection in routine diagnostic laboratories but frequently fail to identify pathogens, particularly in low bacterial burden or antibiotic-exposed samples. While full-length 16S rRNA sequencing improves detection and taxonomic resolution, its adoption is hindered by bioinformatic complexity and operational feasibility. We developed an in-house Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT)-based full-length 16S assay coupled with an open-access, automated analysis pipeline designed for non-specialist staff. In this pilot study, 116 culture-negative clinical samples underwent sequencing, with 86 tested in parallel against outsourced standard-of-care 16S or species-specific PCR. Medical microbiologists, blinded to comparative results, independently assessed clinical relevance. Turnaround time, workflow integration, and cost requirements were also evaluated. Compared to outsourced 16S testing, the in-house workflow demonstrated a 100% positive percent agreement (12/12; 95% CI: 75.7%-100.0%). It significantly expanded clinical diagnostic yield from 14.0% (12/86) to 37.2% (32/86) (p<0.0001), identifying clinically relevant organisms in an additional 20 samples reported as negative by outsourced testing. It enhanced species-level resolution and identified polymicrobial infections (n=8). The NanoPATH pipeline generated clinically interpretable outputs via a single-command workflow and implementation modelling demonstrated that twice-weekly runs would achieve comparable turnaround times to outsourced testing, with cost-neutrality reached at 9 samples per run. An open-access ONT-based 16S workflow which is feasible for routine diagnostic laboratory implementation and operated without specialist bioinformaticians significantly improves pathogen detection from clinical samples. By overcoming analytical and operational barriers, this approach provides a practical framework for integrating sequencing-based diagnostics into standard clinical workflows and improving patient care.

papers.title: Decoding the Rare: Integrative Genomics, Predictive Algorithms and Lipidomics as a Guide for in Lysosomal Storage Disorder Research.
papers.abstract: Lysosomal storage disorders (LSDs) are rare, inherited metabolic conditions characterized by the accumulation of undegraded substrates within lysosomes, leading to progressive multisystemic disease. Clinical and genetic heterogeneity poses significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. This review explores the evolution of LSD diagnostics and highlights the integration of genomic, computational, and biochemical approaches, as well as their implications for personalized medicine. This narrative review is based on a literature search conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science, focusing on diagnostic strategies and biomarker development in LSDs. Traditional diagnostic methods, based on clinical suspicion, enzymatic assays, and substrate quantification, are limited by phenotypic variability and diagnostic uncertainty. Recent advances in next-generation sequencing (NGS), lipidomic profiling, particularly via liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), and in silico variant prediction tools have redefined the diagnostic workflow. When used together, these methodologies allow for more accurate diagnoses, support the classification of variants of uncertain significance (VUS), and guide therapy selection. Biomarkers such as globotriaosylsphingosine (Lyso-Gb3) and glucosylsphingosine (Lyso-Gb1) have become key tools for diagnosing and monitoring specific LSDs, though their performance may vary based on clinical context and patient characteristics. Significant challenges remain, including methodological variability, lack of biomarker standardization, ethical concerns related to genomic testing, and limited clinical integration of multiomic data. The diagnostic landscape for LSDs is shifting toward integrative, personalized approaches. Continued progress will depend on interdisciplinary collaboration, technological development, and harmonized frameworks that ensure equitable access and sustainable innovation, serving as a guiding compass for LSD research.

papers.title: Harigabri-Derived Carbon Dots as FRET Probes for E. coli Analysis.
papers.abstract: Green-fluorescent carbon quantum dots (CQDs) were hydrothermally synthesized from the Mongolian medicine Harigabri, exhibiting uniform size (∼2.5 nm) and strong emission at 521 nm under 468 nm excitation. Based on the fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) between the CQDs (donors) and AgNPs (acceptors), an aptamer-functionalized biosensor (Apt-CQDs/AgNPs) was constructed for selective Escherichia coli detection. Target recognition by the aptamer inhibited FRET and restored fluorescence. The sensor showed a linear response from 9 × 102 to 9 × 107 CFU/mL with a detection limit of 5 CFU/mL. This work highlights Harigabri-derived CQDs as promising nanomaterials for rapid pathogen detection and demonstrates the potential of traditional medicinal resources in biosensing applications.

papers.title: RiboTRAP-seq identifies spatially distinct functions for the anterior and posterior intestine in immune and metabolic regulation in Caenorhabditis elegans .
papers.abstract: The intestine integrates food-derived cues to coordinate organismal physiology, yet the molecular specialization of discrete regions along the intestinal epithelium remains unclear. Here, we generate cell type-specific translatomes of the Caenorhabditis elegans intestine during fasting and refeeding using discrete promoters for the anterior quartet of intestinal cells (INT1) and the remaining eight pairs of intestinal cells (INT2-9). We found that the anterior-most INT1 cells are a translationally distinct intestinal subcompartment that is particularly enriched for immune- and stress response genes. Functional assays using novel INT1-specific genes emerging from this study reveal that these specialized cells play a previously unappreciated role in pathogen avoidance and organismal survival. A second critical function of INT1 cells is their role in sensing and responding to the contents of the gut lumen. We show that luminal pyruvate is the key signal linking bacterial nutrients in the gut to secretion of the gut insulin antagonist INS-7. These findings establish INT1 as sentinel enteroendocrine cells that integrate metabolic and immune cues to couple food status with immune and endocrine responses. Our studies also provide a rich resource for dissecting segment-specific intestinal biology, an overlooked and fertile area for future research.

papers.title: Ultrafast visual detection of Streptococcus suis via HtpsC-targeted LAMP-CRISPR-Cas12a coupled with lateral flow immunochromatography.
papers.abstract: This study describes a rapid, visual detection platform for Streptococcus suis, a significant zoonotic pathogen, by integrating loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) with CRISPR-Cas12a and a lateral flow immunochromatographic strip (LFIA) readout. Targeting the conserved HtpsC gene, specific LAMP primers and a PAM-compliant CrRNA were designed. Following isothermal amplification, the Cas12a/CrRNA complex recognizes the HtpsC amplicon, initiating target-specific cleavage and subsequent trans-cleavage of a dual-labeled ssDNA reporter (FAM-BIO), enabling visual detection on a LFIA; a design which reduces false positives. The optimized assay detected HtpsC-positive S. suis strains within 45 min and achieved a visual detection limit of 1.1 × 10 2 CFU/mL under laboratory conditions, with no cross-reactivity observed against the tested nontarget bacteria. In addition to pure-culture dilutions, the assay was further evaluated using spiked porcine blood samples and achieved similar detection performance, supporting its preliminary applicability in a complex biological matrix. Overall, this study provides an HtpsC-targeted visual detection workflow for screening of S. suis and is expected to be further applied to on-site rapid detection of clinical samples.

papers.title: Host-response biomarker panels for distinguishing selected acute respiratory viral-bacterial co-infections from mono-infections.
papers.abstract: Acute respiratory viral-bacterial co-infections complicate antimicrobial decisions because pathogen detection may not establish whether both organisms are clinically contributing to disease. We synthesized evidence from adult and pediatric acute respiratory infection cohorts, including influenza, SARS-CoV-2, respiratory syncytial virus, adenovirus, and selected mixed-detection febrile illness studies, to evaluate host-response biomarkers for distinguishing co-infection from mono-infection. Conventional C-reactive protein and procalcitonin were most useful as supportive or rule-out markers of bacterial involvement, but lacked sufficient specificity when used alone. Dual-axis strategies that combine antiviral and bacterial-response signals, including MxA/CRP, TRAIL/IP-10/CRP, CD169/CD64, IFI44L/FAM89A, and targeted transcriptomic or proteomic signatures, provided more biologically coherent discrimination of mixed infection states. These findings support prospective validation of integrated host-response panels as rapid decision-support tools for antimicrobial stewardship and clinically meaningful co-infection diagnosis.

papers.title: Microenvironment shapes Staphylococcus aureus phenotypes in children with cystic fibrosis over time.
papers.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus is a common pathogen in children with cystic fibrosis (CF), frequently preceding or coexisting with Pseudomonas aeruginosa . The impact of transient P. aeruginosa infection and therapeutic intervention on S. aureus phenotypic shaping remains poorly understood. We characterized 546 isolates from a longitudinal cohort of sixteen pediatric patients in CF follow-up, either monoinfected or coinfected, over eighteen months. Isolates were grouped into three phenotypic clusters. Monoinfected patients were enriched in a cluster with high pigment and biofilm, whereas transient P. aeruginosa detection was associated with a shift toward reduced pigment and biofilm, while coinfected patients maintained stable phenotypes. Phenotypes were determined by the airway microenvironment rather than by clonal background. In two monoinfected patients, this shift coincided with transient infection and ciprofloxacin treatment with increased MRSA; in vitro , MRSA predominated over MSSA when both P. aeruginosa and ciprofloxacin were present, underscoring the need to monitor S. aureus phenotypic transitions.

papers.title: Network-based characterization of latent co-testing patterns in antimicrobial susceptibility testing.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance depends on antimicrobial susceptibility testing, yet antibiotic panels vary by pathogen cohort, specimen, year, ward, and care setting. We term these empirically reconstructed testing architectures shadow antibiograms: structures that shape which susceptibility results enter surveillance datasets and which resistance relationships can be observed. We analyzed approximately 13 million bacterial isolates from Germany's National Antibiotic Resistance Surveillance system (2019-2023) across six WHO BPPL-aligned operational cohorts. Co-testing networks were constructed using Jaccard, Dice, cosine, and phi-coefficient similarity, evaluated with Fisher's exact tests and Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and partitioned with multi-resolution Louvain community detection. Networks contained three to four dominant co-testing communities; false discovery rate (FDR) retention ranged from 89 to 100% across cohorts and specimen types. Jaccard provided the best balance of coherence, stability, antimicrobial-class alignment, interpretability, and edge retention. This work provides one of the first national-scale empirical characterizations of shadow antibiogram structure, supporting diagnostic stewardship and bias-aware AMR surveillance interpretation.

papers.title: Niche-specific immune and microbial signatures across the healthy upper respiratory tract mucosa.
papers.abstract: Host-microbe interactions in the upper respiratory tract (URT) niches that form the first line of defense against respiratory infections are incompletely understood. We profiled immune and microbial features using minimally invasive samples from 44 healthy adults (20-65 years), including nasopharyngeal (NPS), oropharyngeal (OPS), and mid-turbinate nasal swabs (MTSs), mucosal lining fluid (MLF), and saliva. Multiplex cytokine and antibody assays, 16S rRNA sequencing, and pathogen detection by PCR were performed. Immune and microbial profiles differed by niche: nasal samples showed consistently higher antiviral cytokine levels and Corynebacterium dominance. Oral samples had greater microbial diversity with distinct cytokine and antibody patterns. Saliva and MLF had the highest antibody concentrations, predominantly IgA. Integrated analyses identified site-specific microbe-immune associations. These findings show the feasibility of non-invasive, integrated profiling to uncover compartment-specific host-microbe relationships, providing a scalable framework for respiratory mucosal immunology and microbiome research with applications in infection surveillance and vaccine evaluation.

papers.title: T2T-CHM13 reference genome reduces mapping bias and enhances alignment accuracy at disease-associated variants.
papers.abstract: The T2T-CHM13v2.0 reference genome added previously uncharacterized genomic sequences and improved the accuracy of repetitive stretches compared to former human genome assemblies. By comprehensive allelic variation analysis and read mapping statistics from sequencing reads aligned to hg38 and T2T-CHM13 assemblies in samples encompassing different sequencing designs, we observed that T2T-CHM13v2.0 assembly significantly reduces the reference mapping bias (RMB) and increases read mapping precision at clinically relevant sites, including BRCA1 pathogenic variants. We report the presence of sequence dissimilarities among reference genomes in the proximity of ClinVar annotated variants, suggesting the need for data re-analysis. Analyzing DNA sequencing data from cancer patients, we identified a mean 2.3% increase in variant allelic frequency (VAF) and 0.3% increase in coverage over clinically relevant variants for samples aligned to T2T-CHM13 compared to hg38. Overall, these findings support the implementation of T2T-CHM13 reference for the improvement of sequencing data analyses in the clinical genomic setting.

papers.title: Genomic landscape of sweat gland carcinomas: Clinical applications and future directions.
papers.abstract: Sweat gland carcinomas (SGC) are rare tumors frequently driven by somatic mutations. More than 20 distinct SGC entities are recognized, many of which exhibit overlapping histopathological features, making accurate diagnosis challenging. This review provides a comprehensive overview of SGC entities and summarizes current knowledge of their mutational landscapes to improve understanding of their biology and identify potential therapeutic targets, particularly for aggressive tumors lacking treatment options in advanced stages. Key oncogenic driver mechanisms include high mutational burden, mutational signatures consistent with ultraviolet (UV)-induced DNA damage, dysregulation of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) signaling pathway, and defects in homologous recombination-mediated DNA double-strand break repair. Recurrent, functionally significant somatic alterations have been identified in genes such as TP53, PIK3CA and CDKN2A/B, consistent with their roles in genomic stability, cell signaling and epigenetic regulation. Fusion genes represent a further key feature of SGC. Some fusion genes are entity-specific and serve as molecular hallmarks. Notably, some fusions partners have been identified in several SGC entities, suggesting shared underlying biology. Interestingly, digital papillary adenocarcinoma is the only SGC entity in which oncogenic transformation is mainly driven by a virus (HPV42). This review highlights the need for comprehensive molecular characterization of SGC and discusses the implications for prognosis, risk stratification and therapeutic decision-making. Ongoing case reporting and molecular characterization will be essential to further elucidate the molecular landscape, biological behavior, and therapeutic vulnerabilities of these rare tumors, particularly in carcinomas for which surgical excision alone is unlikely to achieve a curative outcome. Integrating broad molecular profiling with clinicopathological data and establishing systematic registries for rare cancers will be critical to advancing both biological understanding and clinical management of SGC.

papers.title: Thirty years of adjuvant therapy: From treating risk to treating residual disease.
papers.abstract: Over the past three decades, adjuvant therapy for solid tumours has evolved from treatment based predominantly on anatomical recurrence risk towards strategies informed by tumour biology, treatment response, and molecular residual disease. Cytotoxic chemotherapy and endocrine therapy established the curative potential of postoperative systemic treatment, while targeted agents and immunotherapy expanded its efficacy across malignancies. However, matching a drug to tumour biology does not establish whether residual cancer remains, and many patients receive treatment despite having been cured by surgery alone. This Perspective examines the transition from empirical risk reduction towards selective intervention against residual disease. Response-adapted perioperative strategies provide a dynamic assessment of treatment sensitivity and support postoperative escalation or omission in defined settings. Circulating tumour DNA offers a complementary approach, but its strong prognostic value must be distinguished from evidence that biomarker-directed treatment improves outcomes. Contrasting findings from randomised trials demonstrate that neither de-escalation after a negative result nor escalation after a positive result can be generalised across clinical contexts. Future studies should integrate anatomical risk, tumour genomics, pathological response, and longitudinal molecular assessment while prioritising absolute benefit, mature survival outcomes, irreversible toxicity, patient-reported outcomes, and equitable access. They should also distinguish durable eradication from temporary suppression and evaluate treatment omission with the same rigour as intensification. Progress in adjuvant oncology should ultimately be measured by additional cures achieved with less avoidable harm, through the smallest effective intervention supported by validated evidence.

papers.title: Improving RNA secondary structure prediction through expanded training data.
papers.abstract: In recent years, deep learning has revolutionized protein structure prediction, achieving remarkable speed and accuracy. RNA structure prediction, however, has lagged behind. Although several methods have shown moderate success in predicting RNA secondary and tertiary structures, none have reached the accuracy observed with contemporary protein models. The lack of success of these RNA structure prediction models has been proposed to be due to limited high-quality structural information that can be used as training data. To probe this proposed limitation, we developed a large and diverse data set comprising paired RNA sequences and their corresponding secondary structures. We assessed the utility of this enhanced data set by retraining a deep-learning model, SincFold. We find that SincFold exhibited improved performance on a set of previously unseen RNA families, enhancing its capability to predict accurate de novo RNA secondary structures. We additionally implemented Lyra-TransPred, which achieved the highest mean F1 and MCC among the evaluated models while requiring substantially less training time per epoch. The RNASSTR data set provides a substantial advance for RNA structure modeling, laying a strong foundation for the development of future RNA secondary structure prediction algorithms.

papers.title: Multiomics Characterization of HAO2 Expression and Its Clinical Associations in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) exhibits extensive metabolic reprogramming and tumor microenvironmental heterogeneity, contributing to variable outcomes and treatment responses. Hydroxyacid oxidase 2 (HAO2) has been implicated in metabolic regulation, but its clinical and biological relevance in RCC remains incompletely characterized. We integrated transcriptomic, proteomic, genomic, and single-cell RNA-sequencing data to characterize HAO2 expression, clinicopathological associations, metabolic and immune features, and treatment-related outcomes. Exploratory drug-sensitivity associations were evaluated using the Genomics of Drug Sensitivity in Cancer database and pRRophetic. HAO2 expression was consistently reduced across multiple RCC datasets and showed tumor-normal discrimination with area under the curves ranging from 0.73 to 0.97. Low HAO2 expression was associated with advanced stage and shorter overall survival. HAO2 expression was positively associated with metabolic programs and distinct immune microenvironmental features. In the CheckMate-025 cohort, higher HAO2 expression was associated with longer overall survival in both treatment arms. Single-cell analysis showed reduced HAO2 expression in malignant renal epithelial cells. Exploratory pharmacogenomic analysis identified associations between HAO2 expression and drug sensitivity. HAO2 downregulation is associated with advanced disease, unfavorable survival, and distinct metabolic and immune features in RCC. HAO2 represents a candidate tissue-associated biomarker warranting further experimental and prospective validation.

papers.title: Priorities and opportunities for strengthening hygiene and One Health alignment in research, policy and practice.
papers.abstract: Hygiene plays a critical yet under-recognized role in addressing One Health (OH) challenges, including zoonotic disease prevention, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) control, food safety and protection of ecosystem health. Likewise, hygiene research and interventionsgenerally lack an OH perspective, resulting in siloed efforts that inadequately address the human-animal-environment interface. We convened three sessions at global conferences well attended by health professionals working in hygiene or OH. Participants identified gaps and opportunities for hygiene-OH alignment across research, policy and practice at community, national, regional and global levels. An evidence gap identified was research on hygiene approaches to protect ecosystems in programs otherwise focused upon human or animal health. Methodological priorities included harmonizing tools and protocols for pathogen detection, fecal contamination measurement and hygiene behavior assessment; strengthening cross-sectoral data sharing; and developing integrated study designs. Intervention opportunities included engaging local stakeholders, balancing infrastructure and behavior change, adapting existing programs for cross-sectoral relevance and broadening evaluation to include animal and environmental outcomes. Implementation priorities included localized program design and decision-making, regional cooperation for cross-border threats and leveraging surveillance and preparedness infrastructure. Policy priorities included reducing institutional fragmentation, harmonizing standards, and strengthening the roles of hygiene and OH within existing regulatory frameworks. From our synthesis, we present cross-cutting recommendations for strengthening hygiene and OH alignment. Aligning hygiene and OH offers a pathway to more comprehensive and upstream prevention of disease and AMR, supporting coordinated, system-level management of health risks across human, animal and environmental domains and building resilience to emerging health threats.

papers.title: The $100 genome: three platforms reshaping clinical genomics.
papers.abstract: In 2026, three high-throughput sequencing platforms approached the widely publicised sub-$100 30× human genome. Behind these figures, which reflect consumable prices rather than total cost of ownership, the more consequential shift is the end of single-vendor dominance: these systems make comprehensive genomic profiling and multi-omic liquid biopsy feasible in small batches.

papers.title: Cerebrospinal Fluid Cytokine Signatures in Real-Time PCR-Confirmed Acute Bacterial Meningitis: Diagnostic Insights from TNF-α and IL-1β.
papers.abstract: Acute bacterial meningitis (ABM) is a rapidly progressive central nervous system infection where excessive neuroinflammation contributes significantly to morbidity and mortality. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cytokines are key mediators of host immune responses; however, their association with molecular pathogen detection and host inflammatory responses remains incompletely understood OBJECTIVE: To evaluate CSF cytokine responses and their association with molecularly confirmed acute bacterial meningitis METHODS: A total of 246 CSF samples from patients with suspected meningitis, submitted to the department (February 2015 to January 2021) were evaluated. CSF supernatants were used for cytokine quantification, while sediments underwent bacterial culture and Real-time PCR. Cytokines (IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-12p70, IL-6 and IL-10) were measured using cytometric bead array. Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis evaluated diagnostic accuracy. Bacterial DNA was detected in 53/246 (21.5%) samples, with Streptococcus pneumoniae being the predominant pathogen, particularly in children under five. Real-time PCR-confirmed cases showed significantly higher CSF TNF-α and IL-1β levels compared with non-confirmed cases (p = 0.013 and p = 0.033), indicating a predominant pro-inflammatory cytokine. Elevated IL-10 levels suggested concurrent anti-inflammatory regulation. ROC analysis demonstrated modest overall discrimination for TNF-α (AUC = 0.657, p = 0.013) and IL-1β (AUC = 0.605, p = 0.162). However, at an optimal threshold of 0.60 pg/ml, TNF-α achieved 100% specificity, establishing high reliability. Real-time PCR-confirmed acute bacterial meningitis is characterized by a distinct CSF cytokine signature reflecting coordinated pro-inflammatory activation and regulatory immune responses, highlighting CSF TNF-α as a high-specificity adjunctive to molecular assays.

papers.title: Ten simple rules to build genomics capacity for routine laboratory practice in the Global South.
papers.abstract: Developing sustainable genomics capacity in the Global South requires more than technology transfer; it depends on human-centered approaches based on the workflows and existing expertise of laboratory personnel, institutional collaboration, and long-term integration into health systems. Drawing on lessons learned from regional capacity-building initiatives, this article proposes ten simple rules for implementing and sustaining genomics capacity within public health and clinical laboratory settings. These rules emphasize local context, strategic planning, continuous learning, and equitable collaboration. Together, they provide a roadmap for laboratories aiming to transform genomic technologies from research tools for diagnosis, surveillance and decision-making, into routine instruments for public health in low- and middle-income countries.
authors: Arabela Leal E Silva de Melo

papers.title: A broad-host-range Rhizobium rhizogenes strain enables transient expression across diverse crop species.
papers.abstract: Agrobacterium-mediated transient expression has revolutionised plant research, enabling numerous landmark discoveries across diverse areas of plant biology. Yet this powerful approach remains largely confined to solanaceous species, leaving most economically important crop families without a comparable rapid assay platform. Here, we show that an engineered Rhizobium rhizogenes strain, AS109, mediates efficient transient expression across diverse dicot species spanning multiple taxonomic families, consistently outperforming commonly used laboratory agrobacterial strains. Leveraging the broad host range of AS109, we establish a suite of functional assays in faba bean (Vicia faba), including protein localisation, RNA interference-mediated gene silencing, cell-surface elicitor recognition screens, nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat receptor (NLR) activation, and infection cell biology at the host-pathogen interface. We further demonstrate that both singleton NLRs and sensor-helper NLR pairs from Solanaceae retain effector recognition and cell death activity when transferred into faba bean, establishing a rapid platform for evaluating cross-family transferability of disease-resistance genes. AS109 thus provides an accessible and versatile chassis for functional genomics in non-model crops, bridging the widening gap between hypothesis generation and experimental validation across diverse plant species.

papers.title: Moderate-risk variants in hereditary breast and ovarian cancer: seven-year experience from a specialized center.
papers.abstract: Moderate-risk gene variants represent an increasingly recognized component of hereditary breast and ovarian cancer (HBOC) predisposition, yet their clinical interpretation and management remain less standardized than those of high-penetrance genes. This study provides a seven-year real-world evaluation of genetic variants in ATM, BARD1, CHEK2, RAD51C, and RAD51D in individuals undergoing germline testing at a specialized HBOC center, with a particular focus on variant distribution and associated clinical management. We retrospectively analyzed germline testing data from 3416 individuals evaluated at the HBOC center Erlangen between 2018 and 2024. Testing indications included predictive as well as diagnostic and therapeutic testing in the context of breast and gynecologic neoplasms. Variant classifications followed ACMG/IARC (American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics/ International Agency for Research on Cancer) criteria. Clinical recommendations, including participation in the intensified breast cancer surveillance (IBCS) program and risk-reducing surgery, were extracted from structured counseling documentation. (Likely) Pathogenic variants in moderate-risk genes were identified across all clinical subgroups. CHEK2 represented the most frequently altered moderate-risk gene, followed by ATM. In contrast, (likely) pathogenic variants in BARD1, RAD51C, and RAD51D were observed solely among individuals undergoing predictive testing or presenting with breast malignancies. A small subset of individuals carried more than one (likely) pathogenic variant in HBOC susceptibility genes. Most women with moderate-risk variants were enrolled in the IBCS program, although in justified cases participation was withheld based on patient-specific risk factors. An isolated moderate-risk variant generally did not warrant a recommendation for risk-reducing breast surgery. Risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy (RRSO) was primarily discussed with individuals harboring RAD51C or RAD51D variants. Individualized modifications to the recommendations were applied especially in cases with complex genotypes comprising multiple (likely) pathogenic variants. In conclusion, this study demonstrates considerable heterogeneity in germline variants among individuals evaluated for HBOC susceptibility and highlights the particular challenges associated with interpreting moderate-risk gene alterations. The findings underscore the importance of individualized clinical assessment and support the use of real-world data to inform evidence-based surveillance and prevention strategies in hereditary cancer care.

papers.title: Developmental Systems Cardiology III: Measuring Adaptation Across the Lifespan.
papers.abstract: Developmental Systems Cardiology (DSC) conceptualizes congenital heart disease as a lifelong adaptive process shaped by interactions among biological, developmental, psychosocial, environmental, and healthcare systems. As survival has improved, contemporary challenges increasingly include neurodevelopment, psychosocial wellbeing, educational participation, healthcare engagement, and long-term adaptation, requiring multidimensional assessment beyond traditional physiological outcomes. This third article in the DSC series proposes a measurement framework for operationalizing adaptation across the lifespan. Rather than introducing new measurement domains or replacing established assessment recommendations, DSC provides an integrative architecture for linking existing measures across genomics and epigenomics, prenatal exposures, developmental physiology, neurocardiac interactions, family and social determinants, environmental influences, digital phenotyping, and healthcare-system context. Longitudinal measurement serves as a cross-cutting principle for characterizing adaptive trajectories and identifying periods of vulnerability and opportunity. Within this framework, adaptation is a dynamic, measurable process emerging through interactions among individuals, families, healthcare systems, and broader environments. Measurement therefore encompasses developmental functioning, resilience, participation, quality of life, healthcare transitions, and implementation outcomes alongside biological and clinical indicators. Established domain-specific standards, including neurodevelopmental assessment recommendations, can populate this broader architecture. This approach emphasizes integration rather than instrument development, while preserving the specificity and utility of established measures within individual domains. By integrating validated measures across domains, developmental stages, and time, DSC may provide a common language for research, registries, quality improvement, implementation science, and lifespan care. Its proposed contribution lies in organizing multidimensional measurement to better understand how adaptive and maladaptive trajectories emerge and evolve across development.

papers.title: Septic Arthritis of the Knee Caused by Neisseria meningitidis Serogroup Y.
papers.abstract: Neisseria meningitidis is a notifiable pathogen in Japan when isolated from any sterile site. We describe a rare case of primary meningococcal arthritis without meningitis or bacteremia. A 48-year-old man presented with acute septic arthritis of his knee. A synovial fluid analysis using matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry revealed gram-negative diplococci, identified as N. meningitidis. Further antimicrobial susceptibility testing showed the isolate was pan-susceptible, allowing de-escalation from ceftriaxone to ampicillin therapy. The patient recovered fully after surgical drainage and 4 weeks of antibiotic therapy. This case highlights the importance of considering invasive meningococcal disease upon the detection of gram-negative diplococci in synovial fluid.

papers.title: Molecular dynamic simulation of FimD ssDNA aptamers and development of SPR aptasensor for Salmonella.
papers.abstract: For more than a century, non-typhoidal Salmonella has been recognised as a major foodborne pathogen, responsible for human illness underscoring its continued importance to public health. In the current study, we employed molecular dynamic simulation and Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) biosensing based experimental approaches to assess the interaction between the ssDNA aptamers (DFRM13, DFRM110, DFRM29, DFRM33, and DFRM39) and Salmonella FimD usher protein. The docking studies revealed superior binding performance for DFRM13-FimD complex based on its low RMSD (0.7 ± 0.4 nm) and z-score (-1.9) values followed by DFRM39-FimD complex (RMSD: 1.1 ± 0.6 nm, z-score: -1.6). The RMSD, RMSF, Rg, SASA analysis and high number of H-bonds with the ssDNA aptamer (∼18 bonds) observed during 50 ns molecular dynamics simulations revealed that DFRM29-FimD complex also exhibited stable binding interactions. SPR assay optimized with biotinylated aptamers on streptavidin sensors exhibited relatively lower dissociation constant (K D ) or higher affinity for native FimD protein from Salmonella lysates (K D 10 -7 to 10 -8 M) than rFimD (K D 10 -6 to 10 -7 M) due to the cross-over SELEX approach adopted for enriching the aptamers. The DFRM13 demonstrated lowest K D toward FimD in Salmonella thermal lysates (K D 1.24 × 10 -8 M), followed by DFRM39 (K D 4.17 × 10 -8 M) indicating highest binding affinity among other aptamers as determined by SPR interaction kinetics. The sensorgrams with curvatures characteristic of FimD detection was not observed when thermal lysates of non-Salmonella bacteria were examined in the SPR assay, thus confirming the specificity of aptamers for Salmonella detection. Overall, the computational and experimental findings from our study demonstrated potential for possible utilization of the aptamers DFRM13 and DFRM39 in Salmonella diagnostic platforms.

papers.title: Solid-state nanopore and nanochannel platforms for biomarker detection in disease diagnosis: recent advances and perspectives.
papers.abstract: Solid-state nanopore and nanochannel platforms are versatile label-free biosensors that convert biomolecular transport or binding into ionic current signals. This review organizes recent disease-diagnostic applications around a central design chain. Biomarker properties, including size, charge, conformation, abundance, and sample-matrix context, determine whether direct measurement, a molecular-recognition interface, signal amplification, or structural signal translation is required. The selected configuration then shapes the resulting signal characteristics and influences key analytical and translational parameters, including sensitivity, selectivity, dynamic range, throughput, and clinical applicability. Representative advances for protein, nucleic acid, and pathogen biomarkers in cancer, neurological disease, endocrine dysfunction, and communicable disease are critically assessed, including antibody/nanobody and aptamer interfaces, DNA nanostructures, nucleic acid amplification, electro-optical readouts, and machine-learning-assisted analysis. We further identify recurring trade-offs among analytical performance, assay time, matrix tolerance, quantitative robustness, and operational simplicity. Finally, challenges in biofouling, device reproducibility, throughput, standardization, and clinical validation are discussed together with opportunities in integrated materials, data-driven analysis, and portable systems. This framework provides practical design principles for next-generation nanopore and nanochannel diagnostic platforms.

papers.title: Ancient genomes reveal distinct human dispersals and social stratification in the settlement history of western Remote Oceania.
papers.abstract: The settlement of western Remote Oceania involved interactions among deeply divergent populations. Initial settlement ∼3,000 years ago by Lapita-associated, Southeast Asian-related groups was followed by Papuan-related expansions and later sea voyages from Polynesia. We present genome-wide data spanning the past three millennia from the eastern Solomon Islands, Vanuatu, Fiji, and Tonga. We find that the Papuan-related expansion proceeded at a slower pace than the earlier Lapita-associated expansion and reached Fiji through at least two distinct human dispersals, centuries earlier than previously suggested. We provide direct evidence of Polynesian-related gene flow at around 1,000 years ago, giving rise to Polynesian Outlier communities in southern Vanuatu. Finally, we examine an early Fijian community, revealing social practices that preserved wealth/status within a biological kin group with elevated Southeast Asian-related ancestry. Our findings refine the settlement model of western Remote Oceania and highlight the complex interplay of past migrations and community structure.

papers.title: Community-driven advances in computational mass spectrometry: The perspective of EuBIC-MS members.
papers.abstract: Advances in data acquisition, artificial intelligence, and integrative bioinformatics are driving the rapid evolution of computational mass spectrometry, and in turn, transforming modern proteomics, metabolomics, and lipidomics. These developments have greatly increased the scale and complexity of mass spectrometry data, underscoring the importance of evolving accurate, transparent, efficient and reproducible data processing workflows. Addressing these challenges requires collaborative innovation that brings together expertise in software engineering, statistics, and biology. The European Bioinformatics Community for Mass Spectrometry (EuBIC-MS), an initiative of the European Proteomics Association (EuPA), fosters a culture of open, community-driven development through its biennial Developers Meetings and Winter Schools. This commentary summarizes the scientific background and outcomes of the EuBIC-MS Developers Meeting 2025, which took place in Novacella, Italy. Three keynote presentations highlighted major frontiers in the field: deep proteome and phosphoproteome profiling, text mining for protein-protein interaction extraction, and scalable proteomics for AI-driven drug discovery. Seven community-selected hackathons addressed emerging challenges such as single-cell proteomics data analysis, FAIR metadata extraction, deep learning frameworks, R-Python interoperability, and DIA validation. Together, these efforts demonstrate the potential for scientific and technical innovation to arise from open collaboration, and highlight how community-driven initiatives can accelerate progress in computational mass spectrometry. SIGNIFICANCE: Modern proteomics increasingly depends on computational advances to translate complex, high-dimensional data into biological knowledge. The EuBIC-MS Developers Meeting 2025 exemplifies how community-driven collaboration can directly accelerate this process by bringing together experts from bioinformatics, statistics, and experimental proteomics to co-develop open, interoperable, and reproducible analytical tools. By fostering shared software frameworks, transparent benchmarking, and collaborative problem solving, the EuBIC-MS community helps ensure that technological innovation translates into reliable biological insights. This collaborative model strengthens the foundation for quantitative, system-level understanding of proteomes and establishes a sustainable path for integrating artificial intelligence and next-generation data acquisition into routine biological discovery. This commentary shows some current highlights in the field of computational mass spectrometry and community-based approaches undertaken during the most recent Developers Meeting to solve these challenges. The approaches discussed and initiated during the meeting - ranging from deep proteome profiling and phosphosite mapping to text mining, single-cell data analysis, and FAIR metadata extraction - address key bottlenecks that currently limit the biological interpretability and comparability of proteomics data.

papers.title: Cerebrospinal Fluid Transcriptional Immune Pathways Linked to Survival in HIV-Associated Tuberculous Meningitis.
papers.abstract: Tuberculous meningitis (TBM) has approximately 50% mortality in people living with HIV. We investigated differences in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) host immune responses associated with short-term mortality. We enrolled a prospective cohort of adults with HIV-related TBM in Kampala, Uganda. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of bulk CSF RNA was used to detect co-infecting or alternate CNS pathogens and refine diagnoses. Host transcriptomic profiles from the refined cohort were compared between 14-day survivors and non-survivors. Cerebrospinal fluid mNGS reclassified or excluded 14% of participants based on pathogen detection, yielding 110 participants for transcriptomic analysis.Survivors upregulated T-cell receptor signaling (LCK, FYN, LAT), T-cell survival and differentiation (IL7, CD27, IL12RB1), B-cell receptor signaling (CD81, PLCG2, TNFRSF13C), cytotoxic lymphocyte and NK cell genes (KLRD1, ULBP1), TNF signaling, and class I MHC antigen processing pathways, while downregulating neutrophil chemoattractant CXCL1 and classical complement genes C4A and C4B. Unsupervised clustering identified a hypoinflammatory subgroup with significantly elevated mortality. Short-term TBM survival was associated with upregulation of adaptive immunity alongside TNF signaling and IFN-γ-driven class I MHC antigen processing pathways, with concurrent restraint of complement and neutrophil pathways. This supports investigation of adjunctive targeted agents that preserve protective responses while selectively dampening injurious innate pathways.

papers.title: CRISPR-Cas12a biosensing via transcription of crRNA from PCR or LAMP products for pathogen detection.
papers.abstract: Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR)-associated protein 12a (Cas12a) is an RNA-guided nuclease that has been adapted for nucleic acid-based molecular diagnostics. However, the widespread adoption of Cas12-based molecular diagnostics has been limited by dependency of a protospacer adjacent motif (PAM) sequence within the target double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) required to activate Cas12a. To eliminate PAM dependency, we explored a noncanonical activation mode by designing tailed primers for PCR to generate crRNA from amplified target dsDNA products via transcription. The transcribed crRNA, along with a dsDNA activator, then activates Cas12a. We validated this method and named it PCR followed by Transcription And CRISPR-Cas12a (PCR-TRAC). We then developed loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP)-TRAC using tailed primers. Both methods detected Mycobacterium tuberculosis genomic DNA extracted from clinical samples. LAMP-TRAC was more sensitive and faster than PCR-TRAC, detecting as little as four copies/μL of M. tuberculosis genomic DNA within 1 h. We envision that our CRISPR-Cas12-based diagnostic approach could be expanded to become a universal platform for identifying various other nucleic acid targets.

papers.title: Machine vision-integrated portable colorimetric biosensing platform with triple-layered (Pt@ZIF-8) 3 @PDA nanozymes for multiplexed ultrasensitive detection of pathogenic bacteria.
papers.abstract: Simple and in-field detection of multiple pathogenic bacteria is urgently needed. In this work, a biosensor using a nanozyme-based colorimetric immunoassay was developed for sensitive detection of multiple pathogenic bacteria. Firstly, a nanocomposite (Pt@ZIF-8) 3 @PDA-Ab was synthesized based on nanozyme coated with multiple layers of metal-organic frameworks to recognize and probe target bacteria. Additionally, leveraging the catalytic properties of Pt nanoparticles with different substrates (TMB, OPD, AEC, and ABTS), a multicolor sensor array, a portable imaging device, and an in-house coded machine vision algorithm were developed for colorimetric detecting multiple pathogenic bacteria. For single target pathogen detection, this approach exhibits a favorable linear relationship within the range of 10-10 6 CFU/mL, with a detection limit (LOD) as low as 2 CFU/mL for Salmonella Typhimurium. Furthermore, the (Pt@ZIF-8) 3 @PDA-Ab-based biosensor exhibited excellent selectivity and ambient storage stability for as long as 60 days. The colorimetric biosensing platform demonstrates excellent detection capabilities of multiple pathogens bacteria, showing a favorable linear relationship within the range of 10-10 6 CFU/mL, with LOD as low as 10, 7, 5, and 3 CFU/mL for Staphylococcus aureus, Salmonella Typhimurium, Escherichia coli, and Vibrio parahaemolyticus, respectively. The proposed sensor exhibits excellent anti-interference capability (RSD<5.8%). When applied in detecting carrot, lake water and artificial saliva samples, the method demonstrated satisfactory accuracy (RSD<5.8%) for four types of bacteria. This work highlights the synergistic integration of a structurally engineered ambient-stable nanozyme, a multicolor sensor array, and a machine vision-enabled portable device, offering a promising and generalizable strategy for point-of-need pathogen detection in food safety, environmental monitoring, and clinical diagnostics.

papers.title: Illuminating biomarkers: Metal-based strategies and fluorescence nanosensors for clinical monitoring.
papers.abstract: Plasmonic and fluorescence nanosensors have become vital tools for recent diagnostic applications due to their great sensitivity, rapid response, and capacity to determine very small amounts of biological targets. Plasmonic sensors rely on localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR), which occurs when metallic nanostructures, such as gold or silver nanoparticles, generate strong electromagnetic fields on their surfaces. This phenomenon enables sensors to detect changes produced by biomarker or pathogen binding with great accuracy and precision. Recent advances in nanoparticle design and surface modification have improved their selectivity and appropriateness for point-of-care diagnostic devices. On the other hand, fluorescence nanosensors measure changes in fluorescence wavelength or intensity when a target analyte interacts with a fluorescent probe. Advanced fluorescent nanomaterials, including quantum dots, carbon dots, MOF-based fluorophores, and organic dyes, have significantly increased signal stability, biocompatibility, and detection limits. These developments have allowed for the sensitive determination of disease-related analytes such as nucleic acids, proteins, and metabolites. Furthermore, approaches like aggregation-induced emission and fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) have improved the capabilities of fluorescence-based sensing platforms. Both plasmonic and fluorescence nanosensors provide reliable, fast, and simple diagnostic options for early illness diagnosis and clinical monitoring. This review focuses on the operating principles of both approaches, current advances in material design, and their expanding importance in diagnostic applications. This review provides a thorough resource that can successfully support and progress further research and developments in the field, particularly with regard to the applications of comparable nanosensors.

papers.title: PatientPheX: A Full-Text Biomedical Corpus for Patient-Specific Phenotype Information Extraction
papers.abstract: Patient-specific phenotype information extraction identifiers and normalizes phenotype entities and links them with individual patients, supporting rare disease research and genotype-phenotype analysis. However, existing datasets rarely combine full-text biomedical content with detailed annotations of patients, phenotypes, related entities, and their associations. In this work, we present PatientPheX, a corpus for patient-specific phenotype information extraction comprising 200 full-text articles, primarily case reports and case series. The corpus provides mention annotations and normalization for seven biomedical entity types, together with explicit associations between patients and entities across sentences, paragraphs, and sections. Negated findings and composite phenotype mentions are also annotated. Corpus construction combines automated pre-annotation, large language model (LLM)-assisted verification, and manual review and adjudication. Benchmarks cover entity recognition and normalization and patient-phenotype association extraction using gold-standard and predicted entities. The overall document-level entity F1 was 86.95%, while phenotype F1 was 79.33%. The best relation extraction macro-F1 decreased from 84.14% with gold-standard entities to 54.98% with predicted entities, highlighting the combined challenges of phenotype extraction and patient attribution. PatientPheX provides a resource for developing and evaluating patient-centered information extraction methods and supports the construction of structured patient-level knowledge resources for phenotype-driven biomedical research.

papers.title: Constructed Negatives Shape the Evaluation of Sequence-Based Protein--Protein Interaction Models
papers.abstract: Many machine-learning tasks, including representation learning, rely on negative examples that are constructed rather than directly observed. This issue is especially important for protein--protein interaction (PPI) prediction, where experimentally established non-interactions are scarce. PPI models are therefore commonly trained and evaluated against sampled, unobserved protein pairs treated as negatives. We study how this construction affects model comparison. Keeping positives, protein-disjoint splits, class balance, and model selection fixed, we vary training and evaluation negatives independently across six constructions and four sequence-based models, three of which use protein language model (pLM) representations. Changing only the test negatives shifts AUPRC by up to 0.26, and the top-ranked architecture changes with the construction. Negatives matched to true partners in pLM representation space reduce all pLM-based models to near-chance performance, and shuffling partners within each class shows that the original pairing contributes little to AUROC. Constructed training negatives rarely outperform uniform sampling: on external data, they underperform it in 108 of 120 comparisons for the pLM-based models, with gains never exceeding 0.05 AUROC and losses up to 0.23. We release splits, negative-generation procedures, and evaluation code that allow training and evaluation negatives to be varied separately. Our results show that with constructed negatives, model comparisons are not just noisy but systematically sensitive to how negatives are defined, a methodological choice that is often left implicit.

papers.title: New whole slide image analysis method for detection and quantification of hepatocellular vacuolization in European flounder (Platichthys flesus) in multipollutant exposure context
papers.abstract: A new whole slide image analysis method was developed for hepatocellular vacuolization detection and quantification in European flounder (Platichthys flesus) liver. Histopathological quantification allows a better understanding of how contaminants and biotic factors might influence lesion pathogenesis in a multipollutant exposure context. One of the main findings is the significant difference in the extent of the pathology between the polluted and the control sites,with P. flesus sampled in the Seine estuary presenting a higher proportion of tissue affected by hepatocellular vacuolation (6.88 sd. 3.01%) compared to fish sampled in the Canche estuary (5.46 sd. 2.86%). This result is coherent with the previous qualitative histological assessment done on the same histological samples, it helps validate the method and brings new insight into the pathology intensity level with the level of contamination on each site. The other main finding is the potential synergetic effect of the pollutant mixture on the pathology. The multipollutant analysis showed a positive mixture effect on the proportion of tissue affected by hepatocellular vacuolation in fish from the Seine estuary, while this effect is not observed in fish sampled in the Canche estuary. This study highlights the benefits of developing novel bio-image analysis methods for environmental research. Histopathological diagnostic quantification allows a better understanding of the potential factors inducing and exacerbating the pathology, as well as the potential mixture effect in a context of multipollutant contamination.

papers.title: RNAcomp2D: a web tool to execute multiple methods and visually compare predictions of RNA secondary structure
papers.abstract: Ribonucleic acids (RNAs) are involved in many important biological processes. In particular, non-coding RNAs are crucial regulators of cellular processes, playing a significant role in gene expression. RNA secondary structure is key to infer their specific function and for understanding how they interact with other molecules. Many computational models have been developed in the last decade to predict the secondary structure, achieving increasingly higher success rates. However, each new method has its own input-output interface, programming language, computational requirements and, sometimes, a dedicated server to run the model or just a source code in a repository. Thus, nowadays it is very hard to obtain predictions from multiple methods and compare them at once. A unified interface is urgently needed, which allows accessing several methods at the same time, visualizing and comparing predictions among them, and also with a reference structure when available. We introduce here RNAcomp2D, a web-based tool that allows users to enter an RNA sequence, or select one from RNAcentral, and obtain predictions of RNA secondary structures using several state-of-theart methods. Both classical thermodynamic methods and the latest deep learning models are packaged in containers and accessible in an unified website. All the predictions, and the reference structure if available, are shown at the same time in a single graphical interface. Moreover, as new models continue to be developed, this tool is designed to be scalable, allowing the addition of more prediction methods in the future. Web server is available at https://sinc.unl.edu.ar/web-demo/rnacomp2d/. Data and source code are available at https://github.com/sinclab/RNAcomp2D

papers.title: Drug-centric knowledge graph: representing therapeutic modality, pharmacology and multiscale biology
papers.abstract: Biomedical knowledge graphs link targets to mechanisms, diseases and phenotypes, but target-centered representations omit much of what distinguishes therapeutic interventions. We introduce a drug-centric knowledge graph, whose identity model, schema and information-selection priorities are organized around the therapeutic intervention, and a graph built on this design. Each intervention has one identity, linked through relation types shared by all compounds, including target actions, indications, adverse effects, classifications, half-life and direct links to pathways, Gene Ontology concepts, cells and anatomy, and through modality-specific relation types describing small-molecule chemistry, antibody sequences and formats, protein-therapy sequences and antibody-drug conjugate components. Integrating 38 source resources, the graph contains 166,261 nodes of 27 types, 8,106,906 directed edges of 129 relation types and 18,429 compounds in eight therapeutic categories. Construction combines source-specific extraction, compound-identity resolution, language-model-assisted vocabulary and predicate mapping, confidence scoring and connectivity filtering; an expert-reviewed workflow adds investigational therapeutics without altering the base graph. The design offers a reusable template for representing interventions as structured, multimodal objects.

papers.title: ARID5A Is a PERK-Dependent Effector of the Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress Response That Protects Against Steatohepatitis
papers.abstract: Lipotoxic endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress is a fundamental feature of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). ER stress activates adaptive signaling processes that aim to restore ER homeostasis. Yet, depending on the duration, magnitude, and cellular context, sustained ER stress becomes maladaptive and leads to cell death. The regulatory pathways that determine adaptive versus maladaptive ER stress outcomes remain incompletely understood. Here we integrated transcriptomic and chromatin-accessibility analyses in complementary models of proteotoxic and lipotoxic ER stress to identify previously unrecognized regulators of the ER stress response. These analyses identified the dual DNA- and RNA-binding protein AT-rich interaction domain 5A (ARID5A) as an ER stress-responsive gene. ARID5A protein was abundantly expressed in hepatocytes, and ARID5A mRNA and protein were upregulated in palmitate-induced lipotoxic ER stress across multiple hepatocyte models. Using complementary genetic and pharmacological approaches, we demonstrated that ARID5A induction was independent of IRE1 and ATF6 signaling and was attenuated by inhibition of the PERK pathway. To determine the functional relevance of ARID5A in MASH, we employed hepatocyte-directed AAV9-mediated ARID5A overexpression in mice fed a MASH-inducing diet. ARID5A overexpression attenuated steatohepatitis, inflammation, and fibrosis. Together, these findings identify ARID5A as a previously unrecognized PERK-dependent effector of the hepatocyte ER stress response and demonstrate that increasing hepatocyte ARID5A is protective in experimental MASH. This work provides a foundation for defining the mechanisms by which ARID5A regulates hepatocyte stress responses and MASH severity.

papers.title: Nanoscopic Origin of Enhanced Tyrosine-Mediated Water Ordering over Canonical Threonine Motifs in a Bacterial Ice-Nucleating Protein
papers.abstract: Bacterial ice-nucleating proteins (INPs) are known as the most efficient biological heterogeneous ice nucleators. Ice-nucleation ability is conventionally attributed to the threonine-based conserved motifs of {beta} -helical INPs, whereas the role of other conserved motifs remains overlooked. To identify the motif with the highest hydration-ordering ability, a 16-loop model INP and its two mutants are simulated using all-atom molecular dynamics at 260 K, just below the ice nucleation temperature, using the CHARMM36m force field and TIP4P/Ice water model. Among four potential ice-nucleating sites present in four exposed surfaces of the {beta} -helical INP, the glycine-tyrosine-glycine (GYG) motif-associated interface water (IW) exhibits the probability distribution of the Steinhardt bond-orientational and tetrahedral order parameters closest to that of the Ih. The GYG arrange themselves into a ladder-like array of tyrosine hydroxyls, compatible with the Ih-like lattice geometry, suggesting that this motif provides the IW a favorable template for ice-like water organization. The Y-to-phenylalanine mutation produces the largest disruption in IW order compared to the threonine mutations. Although the difference in entropy of threonine-associated IW and Ih is the least among all sites, ice-like hydration ordering near GYG may exceed prior assumptions for a threonine-based ice-nucleating surface. The ordering is collectively determined by lattice compatibility, entropy reduction, hydrophobicity, interfacial geometry, and sequence conservation. The study unfolds a molecular framework of biological ice nucleation and provides a foundation for the rational engineering of more efficient artificial ice-nucleators for applications in climate-related technologies.

papers.title: Quantifying Cancer Clinical Trial Eligibility Using Artificial Intelligence-Based Matching
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop and validate an artificial intelligence-enabled platform that combines efficient screening with explicit eligibility logic by converting unstructured cancer trial criteria into reusable structured queries, and illustrates potential eligibility using synthetic patients. METHODS: We downloaded actively recruiting US interventional treatment trials for advanced/metastatic breast cancer, colon cancer, and non-small cell lung cancer from ClinicalTrials.gov. Medical oncologists created 24 synthetic patient vignettes. A large language model converted trial eligibility criteria into Structured Query Language (SQL) code and patient information into structured records, enabling rule-based matching without further LLM inference. Cancer details and treatment history were considered, but not laboratory results or comorbidities. Validation included physician editing of generated eligibility code for 30 trials and independent assessments by two physicians, followed by consensus adjudication, for eligibility across ten trials. We descriptively summarized potential eligibility by trial characteristics and when varying age, ECOG performance status, sex, and ZIP code. RESULTS: Of 833 candidate trials, 746 met inclusion criteria. Performing matching for all 746 trials took a median of 0.459 seconds per patient, excluding patient-data preparation. Against physician consensus, automated matching agreed on 230/240 patient-trial pairs (95.8%; sensitivity 83.3%, specificity 100%). Across synthetic patients, potentially eligible trials ranged from 10 to 258 without geographic restrictions. Counts decreased with worse performance status and geographic restriction and were relatively stable across ages 30-90. Later-phase, randomized, and molecularly selective trials generally matched fewer vignettes. CONCLUSION: LLM-generated SQL enables rapid, explicit rule-based screening for potential trial eligibility. Evaluation in synthetic vignettes supports feasibility, while missed matches underscore the need for further validation.

papers.title: DAMPA: compositionally optimised probe panel design for targeted metagenomics
papers.abstract: Probe-based enrichment enables highly sensitive direct-from-sample sequencing, and is being rapidly adopted for clinical metagenomics. Targeted metagenomics requires probe panels that capture hundreds of pathogens at comparable efficiency. However, as target sets expand, existing design methods often fail to account for genomic diversity, leading to overrepresentation of conserved sequences. The resulting composition bias reduces sensitivity precisely at the most clinically important and fast-evolving loci, such as antigenic regions, while increasing redundancy and sequencing cost. Here we show that panel composition bias can be minimised through biologically informed sequence compression. We implement the solution in DAMPA, a computationally efficient tool for metagenomic panel design. DAMPA uses pangenome graphs to compress conserved sequences while retaining genetic diversity, then designs probes from graph-node consensuses. In matched tests on six species, DAMPA successfully minimised composition bias, designing panels with up to 75.8% fewer probes than existing methods. In laboratory validation across four species, DAMPA-designed probes achieved sensitive and quantitative detection at Ct>30. In a highly diverse viral genome (Enterovirus A), where commercial panels retained only 7% of expected read depth, DAMPA-designed probes retained 44%, demonstrating improved robustness to sequence diversity and more uniform coverage. DAMPA enables rapid design of compositionally optimised panels that are cheaper to synthesise, while requiring less sequencing for complete genome coverage.

papers.title: A national ecosystem for long-read genome sequencing: Integrating population genomics and rare disease diagnostics in Sweden
papers.abstract: To evaluate the clinical implementation of long-read genome sequencing (lrGS) and establish the population reference resources needed to support its use in diagnostics, we integrate two complementary initiatives: Genome of Sweden (GoS), Sweden's contribution to Genome of Europe (GoE), and the Genomic Medicine Sweden - Rare Diseases (GMS-RD) long-read sequencing pilot. The initial GoS release of 576 individuals provides population-scale maps of genetic and epigenetic variation. Among 485 GMS-RD probands, 161 (33.2%) receive a molecular diagnosis, with lrGS providing added clinical value in 40 (24.8%). As a first-line test, lrGS could have avoided at least 42 follow-up analyses and an additional testing cycle in 7.2% of probands, reducing costs and the burden on patients. By integrating population and clinical long-read genomics, Sweden establishes a national ecosystem for genomic research and clinical diagnostics. Our findings support the clinical implementation of lrGS and offer a scalable model for national collaboration.

papers.title: BanglaDiaHallu: Hallucinations of large language models and the effect of guideline-grounded retrieval-augmented generation in Bangla diabetes question answering
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly consulted for health advice, but they can produce fluent statements that are false or unsupported, known as hallucinations, and this risk is poorly characterised in low-resource languages such as Bangla. We measured hallucinations of locally deployable open-weight LLMs in Bangla diabetes question answering and tested whether retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounded in Bangladeshs National Guideline on Diabetes Mellitus reduces them. Forty patient questions spanning six clinical sub-domains were each answered twice, under zero-shot prompting, by Qwen3.5-9B, TigerLLM-9B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Gemma-4-26B-A4B, and by BanglaDiaRAG, which adds hybrid dense (BGE-M3) and sparse (BM25) retrieval from a physician-reviewed Bangla guideline knowledge base to Qwen3.5-9B. Two physicians rated the 400 de-identified responses by consensus for medical accuracy, completeness, safety, readability and reliability on a 0-1 scale, and responses with accuracy below 0.70 were classified as hallucinated. Hallucination rates were 2.5% for Gemma-4-26B-A4B, 3.8% for TigerLLM-9B, 22.5% for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and 77.5% for Qwen3.5-9B. Guideline grounding lowered the rate of Qwen3.5-9B to 11.3% (difference -66.3 percentage points; 95% CI -76.3 to -55.0) and raised every criterion by 0.24 to 0.38 points (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). BanglaDiaRAG outscored Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on all five criteria and matched or exceeded TigerLLM-9B, but it remained below Gemma-4-26B-A4B in safety, readability and reliability, and its residual errors were specific, confident and potentially harmful. Guideline grounding can turn a weak general-purpose model into a much safer Bangla diabetes assistant, but the choice of base model mattered as much as retrieval and no configuration was free of hallucination, so clinical oversight remains essential before patient-facing use.

papers.title: Performance evaluation and benchmarking across 16 large language model configurations on a large real-world emergency department triage data set
papers.abstract: Background Emergency department (ED) triage is a decision process that determines patient prioritization and resource allocation. Large language models (LLMs) have been proposed as decision-support tools for triage, yet most evaluations rely on curated datasets. Evidence from real-world clinical environments remains limited. The objective of this project was to evaluate the performance and reproducibility of multiple contemporary large language models for Emergency Severity Index (ESI) classification and sectoral allocation (ED vs. urgent care practice, UCP) using a real-world triage dataset. Material and Methods Retrospective cross-sectional benchmarking study conducted at a tertiary academic ED in Germany with an integrated central point of assessment (CPA). The study included all 16,107 walk-in encounters between October 18, 2023, and February 27, 2024. Sixteen configurations were compared on the first 2,000 encounters; GPT 5.1 with high reasoning effort was additionally evaluated on all 16,107 encounters. Data were collected from a structured clinical decision support system capturing presenting complaints, vital signs, and triage decisions recorded by specialized nursing staff. Results The primary outcome was the agreement between LLM-predicted and nurse-assigned ESI levels measured using quadratic-weighted Cohen's kappa. Secondary outcomes included sectoral assignment agreement, misclassification patterns (over- and under-triage), confidence-agreement comparisons, and output reproducibility. In the primary analysis of all 16,107 encounters, GPT 5.1 with high reasoning effort achieved quadratic-weighted kappa = 0.5031 (95% CI 0.4904-0.5158). In the exploratory comparison of 16 configurations on the shared 2,000-encounter subset, quadratic-weighted kappa ranged from 0.180 to 0.860. The Stepwise approach, combining structured model assessments with deterministic ESI mapping, achieved quadratic-weighted kappa = 0.860 (95% CI 0.841-0.878) and 82.70% exact agreement. Most models demonstrated moderate or lower agreement. Sectoral assignment agreement (i.e. ED vs. urgent care practice, UCP) was uniformly low (kappa of 0.304 or lower).
